name: Elena Marsh
quote: I don't chase perfect light. I wait for honest light.
intro: Elena grew up in a small fishing town on the Carolina coast, where her grandfather ran a bait-and-tackle shop at the end of the pier.
story: At eleven she borrowed his battered Pentax and burned through a whole roll of film on tide pools. Most of it was out of focus. One frame, a hermit crab caught mid-shuffle, hung on her bedroom wall for a decade.

She studied marine biology and spent four years looking at the coast through a microscope, then found herself photographing a friend's wedding on a grey, drizzly morning in 2015. Nothing about it was perfect, and it was the best work she had ever made. Grey light, she realised, tells the truth.

A year later she opened Saltmarsh Photo Co. in a loft above a sailmaker's shop, named for the marsh behind her grandfather's pier, a place where the land and the sea have never quite made up their minds. Ten years on, the loft is a little less drafty, the team is two photographers and one studio dog, and she still checks the tide table before she checks her email.
timeline: Borrows her grandfather's Pentax and photographs every tide pool on the beach.
Studies marine biology. Learns to be very patient with very small things.
Photographs a friend's wedding in the drizzle and never looks back.
Opens Saltmarsh Photo Co. above a sailmaker's loft.
Two photographers, one studio dog, still waiting on the tide.
facts: 6:12 a.m., just before the sun clears the pier
Biscuit, a beagle with strong opinions
Black, from a thermos older than the business
beforeSession: Wear something you can sit in the sand in, bring a jacket for after sunset, and don't worry about posing. I'll talk you through everything, and the best photographs usually happen when you've stopped trying.
